_note: Register: krama for every sentence, bare stems on buttons (Èkspor, Simpen, Batal, Tutup), matching the pack's own level -- the studio addresses one reader and a Javanese interface that addressed them in ngoko would be the same discourtesy a ngoko card is. Terms of art: a printed face is sisi and a sheet is lembar, so "4 faces / 2 sheets" is "4 sisi / 2 lembar"; duplex is bolak-balik; typeface is jinis aksara; romanisation is romanisasi; the respelling field is Cara maos and the literal gloss Teges harfiah; "glossed into" is Teges ing basa. The divider is pamisah and "garis" is kept for the printed hairline (warn.hairline-too-thin), which is ink where the divider is not. Interpolation: Intl.DisplayNames hands Javanese the bare ethnonym ("Inggris", "Jepang", "Jawa"), which is a country or a people on its own, so every template that takes {language} carries the head noun basa in front of it -- "Ing basa {language}", "Basa {language} dipunginakaken ing {regions}", "kertu basa {language}", "panduan basa {language}". This is the same repair the Indonesian catalogue records, and it is needed here for the same reason and on the same six templates. Romanisation systems keep their Latin names -- Javanese has no settled form for Hepburn, Kunrei-shiki, McCune-Reischauer or Hunterian, and ALA-LC, BGN/PCGN, IAST and RTGS are standards initialisms -- except roman.rr, which is calqued as "Romanisasi Révisi". Orthography follows the pack: é = [e], è = [ɛ], bare e = [ə].
